title: Arbitrary-Round Security for Single-Key Key-Alternating Ciphers
summary: Existing results cover only limited round counts; it remains open whether key-alternating ciphers using a Chen et al.-style single-key sub-key schedule can be proved secure for arbitrarily many rounds.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether key-alternating ciphers instantiated with a single-key sub-key schedule, as in Chen et al., can be proved secure for an arbitrary number of rounds; that is, whether security can be established for any round count beyond the limited-round results discussed for key-alternating ciphers.

scope.domain: Security of key-alternating block ciphers using single-key sub-key schedules.
parameters: Round count: the target is security for an arbitrary number of rounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove security for any number of rounds when the key-alternating cipher uses a single-key sub-key schedule as in Chen et al.

citations.label: Tight Security for Key-Alternating Ciphers with Correlated Sub-Keys

progress.summary: The source frames this as the ultimate extension beyond limited-round security results, asking whether a Chen et al.-style single-key schedule can support an arbitrary number of rounds.
citation_labels: Stefano Tessaro et al., Tight Security for Key-Alternating Ciphers with Correlated Sub-Keys
